MANAGEMENT OR DIAGNOSTIC PLAN
Ideally participants should consider obtaining a 12-lead ECG in the clinic/office while the patient is there (if requested this will be provided).
Participants should also refer the patient for a stress test and should consider whether they would manage this patient in the inpatient or outpatient setting.
MK:
Diagnosis with support from positive and negative history and PE findings
Stable Angina (+ intermittent chest pain with exertion, +associated shortness of breath, + pain relieved with rest, + smoking history, Tums and Prilosec not palliative, high stress job, history of hypertension and diabetes contributing factors)

Differential with support from positive and negative history and PE findings
Unstable Angina (intermittent chest pain with exertion and associated shortness of breath, - pain relieved by rest)
Acute Myocardial Infarction (+ intermittent chest pain with exertion and associated shortness of breath, - pain relieved by rest)
GERD ( +burning pain, - for pain after eating or pain when lying down)
Peptic Ulcer Disease (+ pain/burning in chest, - nausea, vomiting, excessive gas)
Pulmonary Embolism (+ recent flight, - sudden onset of shortness of breath, shortness of breath and pain resolves with rest, Oxygen saturation is normal, heart rate is 78)
Aortic Stenosis (- murmur, - lightheadedness, - fainting)
Costochondritis (- pain with deep breathing or cough, not reproducible with palpation)
